item.title: Nicki Minaj fans say they’re leaving Democrat Party as rapper’s politics spark backlash and praise
item.description: Nicki Minaj fans are reportedly switching to the Republican party after her Trump support, with viral social media posts showing "Barbz" leaving the left.

item.title: Tulsi Gabbard denies wrongdoing over delayed whistleblower complaint referral to Congress members: 'Baseless'
item.description: A classified whistleblower complaint alleging wrongdoing by Tulsi Gabbard sparked a political battle over national security and congressional oversight.

item.title: Fireworks fly as hooded protesters clash with police after Olympics open in Milan
item.description: Some protests in Milan turned violent as hooded demonstrators lobbed fireworks at police during Winter Olympics demonstrations. Five people were arrested after clashes.

item.title: Over 5,000 cold-stunned iguanas removed in two days during state's record freeze
item.description: Over 5,000 invasive green iguanas were captured in Florida during a recent freeze that left the reptiles cold-stunned and temporarily paralyzed on the ground.

item.title: Fire-juggling unicyclist caught on camera blocking traffic in major roadway as police intervene
item.description: A Colorado police department was stunned when a fire-juggling unicyclist turned a busy intersection into street theater, saying it was "not on our Bingo card."

item.title: Guy Fieri champions veterans and military who 'keep this country free' in exchange with Kevin Costner
item.description: "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives" star Guy Fieri praises Kevin Costner's work with veterans, calling him "the real deal" for his Santa Barbara program.

item.title: Chaos ensues at UNC-Duke game after fans storm court too early, evacuate for final 0.4 seconds
item.description: UNC fans celebrated early after a last-second three, but officials reset the clock before the Tar Heels beat Duke 71-68 in their biggest comeback over the Blue Devils since 2001.

item.title: Federal appeals court upholds Trump mass detention policy for illegal immigrants
item.description: A federal appeals court ruled that the Department of Homeland Security can lawfully detain illegal immigrants nationwide without bond hearings, delivering a major legal win for the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement policy.
